You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## task-81043219 — fill enclosed cavities by area parity (solved)

**Verified result:** For each enclosed background-color cavity bounded by a same-color outline, fill its interior with 7 when the cavity's number of cells is odd, or 2 when even. Preserve every outline and all other cells. Exact test output was scored CORRECT.

**Test instance:** background 3. Enclosed interiors: color-1 3x3 cavity (area 9) -> 7; color-0 center 1x1 (area 1) -> 7; two color-6 1x1 cavities -> 7 each; color-5 1x1 cavity -> 7. Other cells unchanged.

**Demonstration evidence:** Across two pairs, enclosed cavities with dimensions 1x1, 3x3, and 5x5 (odd cell area) were filled with 7; cavities 2x2 and 4x4 (even cell area) were filled with 2. The rule is parity of cavity area, not outline color or overall object size. Frames can be separate components/objects; identify each closed interior independently. Keep output dimensions and every non-cavity cell identical to input.

**Process note:** One speculative submission failed; the following parity-based submission was explicitly scored CORRECT. For recurring variants, compute each enclosed region's area and set its fill to 7 for odd, 2 for even. Request a demo rather than guessing if cavity enclosure or rule differs.

**Test layout:** Color 3: vertical segment at far right (rows 3–5, col 10), vertical segment (rows 7–12, col 9), horizontal pair (row 15, cols 4–5). Color 4: one connected large lower/right shape (rows 13–20, chiefly col 7 plus upper bar across cols 7–10). Color 1: singleton (9,3), vertical pair (19–20,1), singleton (19,9). The correct target is the singleton at (9,3); recolor it to 4 only.

**Demo observations:** Eight demos were provided; outputs alter selected objects/cells while leaving the rest unchanged. Examples: demo 1 recolors a lower-left color-4 shape to 1; demo 2 recolors a 2x2 color-4 object to 2; demo 3 recolors a color-9 object to 5; demo 4 recolors a color-8 object to 7; demo 5 recolors a color-9 component to 6; demo 6 recolors a color-1 shape to 0; demo 7 recolors part of a color-8 object to 6; demo 8 recolors a color-7 shape to 2. A grid with uniform background contains two horizontal bars of the same color: one spans the entire row, the other is truncated from the left. Extend the truncated bar to the right edge, filling only the background cells after its endpoint with color 1. Preserve the complete bar, existing segment, background, and all other cells.
